new_statements.quote: The prevailing word pattern of Brũ is CVC/CCVC in which CVC represents a non-stressed, non-obligatory pre-syllable and CCVC a stressed, obligatory main syllable. The pre-syllable exhibits a high degree of vowel neutralization with very little vowel contrast, whereas the main syllable demonstrates full contrast between all vowels.
new_statements.citation: Phillips, Richard L., John Miller & Carolyn Miller. 1976. The Brũ vowel system: alternate analyses. Mon-Khmer Studies 5: 203-217.
new_statements.locator: p. 217, note 4 (endnotes to the introduction); dialect statement in note 3 on the same page
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (15 pages, no text layer) and rendered page 15 (= MKS 5 p. 217) to an image; also read the scanned file (lines 754-800). Note 4 on p. 217 reads exactly as quoted: "The prevailing word pattern of Brũ is CVC/CCVC in which CVC represents a non-stressed, non-obligatory pre-syllable and CCVC a stressed, obligatory main syllable. The pre-syllable exhibits a high degree of vowel neutralization with very little vowel contrast, whereas the main syllable demonstrates full contrast between all vowels." (The scanned renders "Brũ" as "Brii"; the page image has "Brũ", so the reader's quote is the verbatim page text.) Note 3 on the same page: "Brũ is a language of the Mon-Khmer family. The dialect…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Words are sesquisyllabic: an optional unstressed pre-syllable (CVC, with neutralized vowel) plus an obligatory stressed main syllable (CCVC). Stress therefore always falls on the main (final) syllable of the word; in monosyllables it is the only syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. The same paper (p. 205) adds that the first/second register contrast has nothing to do with pitch: register-pairs are said on the same pitch in isolation and in connected speech.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('word pattern'); based on the Bru of Hướng Hóa district, Quảng Trị province, South Vietnam (the Vân Kiều dialect), i.e. Eastern Bru proper. The Thailand-side statements (Thongkum 1980 p. 222, Miller & Miller 1994 p. 45) give the same rule for Western Bru / So-Bru dialects.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes the Bru of Hướng Hóa district, Quảng Trị province (South Vietnam), i.e. the Vân Kiều dialect of Eastern Bru [bru], east2332.), which Glottolog files as Western Bru (west2397) or So, not east2332; Thongkum explicitly says her variety is not the dialect studied by Miller in Vietnam.

sources.locator: p. 217, note 4 (endnotes to the introduction); dialect statement in note 3 on the same page
sources.note: Note 4, p. 217: the prevailing word pattern is CVC/CCVC, CVC a non-stressed, non-obligatory pre-syllable and CCVC a stressed, obligatory main syllable; pre-syllable vowels heavily neutralized. Dialect of Hướng Hóa district, Quảng Trị (= Vân Kiều). Also states register differences carry no pitch (p. 205).

sources.citation: Miller, John D. & Carolyn P. Miller. 1994. Notes on phonology and orthography in several Katuic Mon-Khmer groups in northeast Thailand. Mon-Khmer Studies 24: 27-51.
sources.note: Section 5.1, p. 45: all six So/Bru dialects of NE Thailand are sesquisyllabic, a non-stressed non-obligatory pre-syllable followed by a stressed obligatory main syllable. Not the Quảng Trị dialect (Thailand So-Bru groups; identity mostly Western Bru/So).

sources.citation: Theraphan L. Thongkum. 1980. The distribution of the sounds of Bruu. Mon-Khmer Studies 8: 221-293.
sources.note: Section 2, p. 222: 'Main syllables, of the structure C(C)V(C) or c(c)V(C), always receive stress'; presyllables are N or CV(C). Variety: Ban Woen Buek, Khong Chiam, Ubon Ratchathani, Thailand, explicitly 'not the same dialect as the one spoken in Vietnam which was studied by Miller' = Western Bru (west2397).
